extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Independent, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in relevant majors were recruited as annotators. They collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources or created new questions based on expertise. Annotators adhered to copyright regulations, avoided sources prohibiting redistribution, and selected questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination. Annotations included question text, options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed by the authors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the relevant majors.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset has a version change log (V1 to V4 documented in the paper). A live-updating leaderboard is maintained at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark relates to Expert AGI, which marks a critical milestone that could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Monitoring progress towards Expert AGI is of intellectual and societal importance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
